runs.text:
Eighty-seven years ago our forebears founded a new nation here, built on liberty and on the idea that all men are equal.

Now a civil war tests whether that nation, or any nation built this way, can last. We stand on a great battlefield of that war. We have come to give part of this field as a resting place for those who died so the nation might live. That is right and fitting.

But we cannot truly dedicate this ground, nor consecrate it, nor make it holy. The brave men who fought here, living and dead, have already done that, far beyond our power to add to or take away. The world will barely note, and soon forget, what we say today. It will never forget what they did. It falls to us, the living, to finish the work they began so well. It falls to us to commit to the great task ahead: to draw from these dead greater devotion to the cause for which they gave everything; to resolve that they shall not have died for nothing; that this nation, under God, shall see a new birth of freedom; and that government of the people, by the people, for the people, shall not vanish from the earth.
